title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship

title: Harvard Medical School Fellowship in Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition
inst: Boston Children's Hospital (Harvard Medical School)

title: Pediatric Endocrinology Fellowship
inst: Boston Children's Hospital (Harvard Medical School)

Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Three-year pediatric endocrinology fellowship combining inpatient and outpatient clinical training with a structured curriculum including the Endocrine Summer Series, Fundamentals of Endocrinology and a fellows' journal club.

title: Pediatric Rheumatology Fellowship Training Program
inst: Boston Children's Hospital (Harvard Medical School)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page

Positions: Most years two fellows (per year, as stated: 'we have two fellows')
Summary: ACGME-accredited pediatric rheumatology fellowship with ambulatory and inpatient training, musculoskeletal ultrasound and joint injection training, and mentored basic or clinical research in the second and third years.

title: Developmental-Behavioral Pediatrics Fellowship
inst: Boston Children's Hospital (Harvard Medical School)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Comprehensive three-year ACGME-accredited DBP fellowship with clinical, didactic and research training, including an intensive research experience at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health.

title: Pediatric Hospital Medicine Fellowship
inst: Boston Children's Hospital (Harvard Medical School)

Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Funding: Fully funded master's degree through Harvard schools during years 2-3
Summary: One of the oldest pediatric hospitalist programmes in the US, offering a three-year fellowship with a fully funded Harvard master's degree and training in medical education, QI, research and health equity.

title: Pediatric Critical Care Medicine Fellowship Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of residency training in pediatrics
Application method: ERAS online application, personal statement and three letters of recommendation; positions offered through the match
Summary: Founded in 1968, CHOP's PCCM fellowship trains independently practising paediatric intensivists and leaders in patient care, research, education and quality improvement, with options to combine with other subspecialties.

title: Pediatric Endocrinology Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Three-year programme preparing pediatricians for academic and clinical careers in pediatric endocrinology and diabetes, with a clinical first year followed by patient-oriented or laboratory research (or a clinical track).

title: Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Department: Division of Cardiac Critical Care Medicine
Eligibility: Board certified in Pediatrics and board eligible/certified in Pediatric Critical Care Medicine, Pediatric Cardiology, Pediatric Anesthesiology or Neonatology
Summary: One-year advanced clinical fellowship in one of the world's largest cardiac intensive care units dedicated to children with critical cardiac disease, preparing fellows for leadership in pediatric cardiac critical care.

title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Duration: Not stated on official page for core track; combined PEM-Global Health track is 4 years
Eligibility: Completion of training in ABP- or ABEM-approved programmes in Pediatrics or Emergency Medicine
Positions: Anticipated 5 positions annually (4 PEM and 1 combined PEM/Global Health track)
Summary: One of the first PEM fellowships in the US, based in a Level 1 Pediatric Trauma Center ED caring for more than 100,000 children each year, with an optional four-year combined Global Health track.

title: Pediatric Cardiology Fellowship Training Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Positions: 6 first-year clinical fellowship positions (one additional slot may be open for ROTC/military-sponsored applicants)
Summary: One of the nation's oldest and largest pediatric cardiology fellowships, with advanced training options in noninvasive imaging, catheterization, electrophysiology, ACHD, heart failure-transplant, pulmonary hypertension, pathology and research.

title: Pediatric Rheumatology Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Eligibility: Physicians trained in pediatrics
Summary: Three-year programme combining a clinical year with at least two years of scholarly work in basic, translational or clinical research, with participation in multidisciplinary uveitis, lupus nephritis and immune dysregulation clinics.

title: Pediatric Nephrology Fellowship Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Three-year programme providing clinical and research skills for academic pediatric nephrology, including renal biopsy, acute and chronic dialysis, and optional Master's or certificate training at the University of Pennsylvania.

title: Pediatric Hospital Medicine Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Duration: 2 (+1) years: ACGME requirements in 2 years plus an optional track year
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Two-plus-one-year fellowship training future leaders in pediatric hospital medicine, with track-specific second and third years including Master's-level training at the University of Pennsylvania.

title: Pediatric Neurocritical Care Fellowship Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Department: Divisions of Critical Care Medicine and Neurology
Eligibility: Critical Care track: completed pediatrics residency and pediatric critical care fellowship, board eligible/certified. Neurology track: completed child neurology residency, board eligible/certified
Positions: Up to 1 Critical Care track and up to 1 Neurology track trainee each year
Summary: One-year clinical fellowship developing specialty training in pediatric neurointensive care for board-certified/eligible pediatric intensivists and child neurologists.

title: Pediatric Extracorporeal Life Support (ECLS) Fellowship Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Department: Division of Critical Care Medicine / Cardiac Critical Care
Eligibility: Board eligible/certified in Pediatric Critical Care Medicine, or Pediatric Cardiology with an additional 1-year Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care fellowship; board certified in General Pediatrics; USMLE certification or equivalent; PALS and ACLS
International applicants: Not stated on official page (USMLE certification or equivalent required)
Visa support: Applicants must have visa eligibility for training, if needed
Summary: One-year clinical fellowship mentoring board-certified/eligible pediatric intensivists and cardiac intensivists in the techniques, management and decision-making of extracorporeal life support.

title: Pediatric Allergy and Immunology Fellowship Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Three-year programme preparing pediatricians for academic careers in allergy and immunology, with a clinical first year and research years, at a WAO Center of Excellence with the largest food challenge programme in the US.

title: Academic General Pediatrics Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Application method: Via the Academic Pediatric Association (APA) website
Funding: Two years of stipend, benefits, tuition and an allowance for travel and other training expenses
Summary: Two-year research fellowship within the University of Pennsylvania's Primary Care Research Training Program, culminating in a Master's in Clinical Epidemiology or Health Policy Research, focused on health equity and primary care research.

title: Pediatric Cardiology Fellowship
inst: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago / Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed accredited pediatric residency; ABP board-certified or board-eligible to sit the exam during the first year of fellowship
International applicants: International medical graduates welcome; must hold valid ECFMG certificate and documentation of US citizenship, green card or J-1 visa (McGaw Medical Center requirements)
Application method: ERAS (programme number 3251611013); applications open July of the year before start; CV, personal statement, photo, USMLE/COMLEX scores, transcript, 3-4 letters
Visa support: J-1 per McGaw requirements; programme does not sponsor H-1B visas
Licence requirement: Must meet State of Illinois requirements for temporary medical licensure
Summary: Pediatric cardiology fellowship in existence since 1964 that develops academic pediatric cardiologists, accepting four categorical fellows per year for 36 months of training.

title: Pediatric Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago / Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited pediatrics residency and eligible for ABP General Pediatrics certification
International applicants: Non-US citizens need a valid visa and authorisation to work in the United States
Application method: ERAS (CV, personal statement, 3 letters, transcript, USMLE transcript); NRMP fall pediatric subspecialty match; interviews August-November
Visa support: Non-US citizens need a valid visa and authorisation to work in the US (sponsorship type not specified on programme page)
Licence requirement: Must meet State of Illinois requirements for temporary medical licensure
Summary: Three-year PCCM fellowship providing comprehensive training in the scientific and clinical practice of pediatric critical care medicine.

title: Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine Fellowship
inst: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago / Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited pediatric residency; ABP board-certified or board-eligible; sufficient NICU experience (at least three neonatology rotations highly recommended)
International applicants: Graduates of schools outside the US and Canada need qualifying examinations (USMLE, FMGEMS, TOEFL, FLEX) and translated credentials; non-US citizens need a valid visa and work authorisation
Accreditation: Accredited by the Residency Review Committee for Pediatrics
Application method: ERAS during the fall pediatric subspecialty match
Visa support: Non-US citizens need a valid visa and authorisation to work in the US
Licence requirement: Must meet eligibility requirements for a temporary Illinois medical license
Summary: Three-year neonatal-perinatal fellowship with rotations at Lurie Children's and Prentice Women's Hospital, training fellows as excellent clinicians and academic neonatologists.

title: Pediatric Endocrinology Fellowship
inst: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago / Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed accredited pediatric residency; ABP board-certified or board-eligible
International applicants: IMGs welcome; must hold valid ECFMG certificate and documentation of US citizenship, green card or visa per McGaw requirements
Application method: ERAS (programme number 3261621060), from July of the year before start; interviews August to October/early November
Visa support: Visa per Northwestern McGaw Medical Center requirements (type not specified on programme page)
Licence requirement: Must meet eligibility requirements for a temporary Illinois medical license
Summary: ACGME-accredited three-year pediatric endocrinology fellowship cultivating well-rounded leaders for academic, public health, advocacy and industry careers.

title: Pediatric Pulmonology Fellowship
inst: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago / Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine

Application method: ERAS; NRMP Fall Match; virtual interviews
Visa support: Does not currently accept applicants seeking an H-1B visa
Licence requirement: Must meet State of Illinois requirements for temporary medical licensure
Summary: Three-year fellowship at the largest pediatric pulmonary practice in Chicago, accepting one fellow per year for individualised training.

title: Child Abuse Pediatrics Fellowship
inst: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago / Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited pediatrics residency and board-eligible in pediatrics
Application method: ERAS general application with transcripts, CV, personal statement and three letters (one from residency programme director)
Positions: Funding for at least one fellow each year (3-4 fellows at a time)
Licence requirement: Must meet eligibility requirements for a temporary Illinois medical license
Summary: One of the larger child abuse pediatrics training programmes in the US, preparing fellows for academic and leadership roles in child abuse pediatrics.

title: Pediatric Rheumatology Fellowship
inst: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago / Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Accreditation: Training content in accordance with ACGME Residency Review Committee for Pediatrics guidelines
Positions: Generally one fellow every three years; up to one new fellow per year when funding allows
Summary: Three-year rheumatology fellowship weighted toward clinical training in the first year and research in years two and three.

title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship

Licence requirement: Must meet eligibility requirements for a temporary Illinois medical license
Summary: One-year cardiac intensive care fellowship training fellows since 1998, with six months on the cardiac ICU service and tailored rotations depending on cardiology or critical care background.

title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship

Accreditation: Fully accredited by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada

Licence requirement: Licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of British Columbia (CPSBC) required (postgraduate/educational licence for fellows; CPSBC English-language proficiency requirements apply)
Summary: Royal College-accredited two-year pediatric critical care programme based at BC Children's Hospital, with training divided between the CICU and MSICU plus research and electives.

title: Academic Pediatrics Fellowship
inst: Stollery Children's Hospital / University of Alberta
Eligibility: Not stated on official page

Accreditation: Not accredited by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada

Accreditation: Not accredited by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada

title: Interventional Catheterization Fellowship
inst: Stollery Children's Hospital / University of Alberta

title: Fetal and Neonatal Cardiology Fellowship

Summary: Training in fetal and pediatric echocardiography at a programme performing over 1,800 fetal echocardiograms a year, preparing fellows to function independently as fetal cardiologists and pediatric echocardiographers.

title: Medical Training Initiative (Paediatrics) - MTI(p)
inst: Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH)
Eligibility: Paediatricians currently in training outside the UK/EEA, overseas at time of applying with no UK/EEA residency rights; practising clinically in an AoMRC priority country; IELTS Academic minimum 7.0 in each band and 7.5 overall (or OET equivalent); GMC-accepted primary medical qualification verified via ECFMG; minimum 3-year postgraduate paediatric qualification accepted by RCPCH or full MRCPCH; 36 of last 60 months and 10 of last 12 months in direct clinical practice; intention to return home
International applicants: Yes - designed specifically for international medical graduates from outside the UK/EEA (priority to World Bank Low Income and Lower Middle Income countries)

Positions: Posts usually at middle-grade level (induction up to 6 months at ST3, then ST4-5 level)
Visa support: RCPCH provides GMC registration sponsorship and recommendation for a Temporary Work - Government Authorised Exchange visa Certificate of Sponsorship (issued by AoMRC)
Summary: RCPCH-quality-assured scheme giving paediatricians from outside the UK/EEA up to two years of postgraduate training in the NHS, with College sponsorship for GMC registration and visa.

Licence requirement: Temporary Registration with the Singapore Medical Council (SMC) required (SMC fees S$300 application + S$550 practising certificate)
Summary: One-year broad-based clinical fellowship in paediatric nephrology including renal biopsy, peritoneal dialysis and CVVH, developing independent and competent paediatric nephrologists.

title: International Clinical Fellowship Programme (ICFP) in Paediatrics
inst: Royal College of Physicians of Ireland (RCPI) - Faculty of Paediatrics
Duration: Varies by specialty: e.g. General Paediatrics and PEM up to 3 years; Endocrinology, Gastroenterology, Allergy & Immunology, Developmental Paediatrics 2 years; Infectious Diseases and Respiratory 12-24 months; Rheumatology up to 3 years
Eligibility: Primary medical degree taught in English; structured internship; at least one year post-residency experience in chosen specialty; completed 4-5 year national residency programme with exams (e.g. Saudi or Arab Board); eligible for Irish Medical Council Supervised Division registration; IELTS Academic 7.0 overall (6.5 each) or OET B
International applicants: Yes - programme is for international doctors who are citizens of Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia or the UAE; must be government-sponsored (self-sponsored candidates not accepted); MRCPI/MRCP UK holders given priority
Licence requirement: Eligibility for registration with the Medical Council of Ireland (Supervised Division)
Summary: RCPI Faculty of Paediatrics programme offering sponsored international doctors structured clinical training in leading Irish hospitals across paediatric specialties including PEM, neonatology, cardiology, endocrinology, gastroenterology, ID, respiratory and rheumatology.

title: Post-CSCST Fellowship in Paediatric Critical Care Medicine
inst: Children's Health Ireland (CHI at Crumlin and Temple Street)
Department: Paediatric Critical Care Units, Children's Health Ireland
Duration: 1 year (training year based primarily at CHI Crumlin with neuro-critical care module at CHI Temple Street)
Eligibility: CSCST or equivalent in base specialty by commencement and one year of paediatric critical care training; or wish to advance interest, training and experience in PCCM
Accreditation: PCCM training in CHI PCCUs is recognised by the Joint Faculty of Intensive Care Medicine of Ireland (JFICMI)
Summary: Supra-specialty competency-based fellowship in paediatric critical care across Ireland's tertiary PCCUs (about 1,500 admissions a year), which will amalgamate into a 42-bed PCCU at the new National Children's Hospital.

title: Postgraduate Training in Paediatric Intensive Care Medicine
inst: Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève (HUG) - Hôpital des enfants
Department: Unité des Soins Intensifs Pédiatriques et Néonatals, Service de Néonatologie et de Soins Intensifs Pédiatriques
Duration: Individualised training plan; includes optional 6-12 month rotations in partner centres (e.g. HUG adult ICU, anaesthesia, paediatric cardiology, CHUV PICU)
Eligibility: Prior postgraduate training in paediatrics strongly desired; for chef de clinique posts prior intensive care or anaesthesia experience is essential; French (spoken and written) at C1 level required (HUG institutional obligation)
International applicants: Applications accepted from doctors seeking specific training, Swiss or international (per training concept)
Accreditation: Postgraduate training concept registered with the Swiss Institute for Medical Education (SIWF/ISFM)
Application method: Application to the head of the PICU unit (address/email in training concept)
Summary: SIWF-registered postgraduate training in paediatric intensive care at HUG's multidisciplinary PICU, a centre for highly specialised medicine caring for patients from extreme prematurity to 16 years, including congenital heart disease and paediatric liver transplantation.

title: Postgraduate Training in Paediatric Intensive Care Medicine
inst: Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Vaudois (CHUV)
Department: Unité Médico-Chirurgicale de Soins Intensifs Pédiatriques (SIP), DFME
Duration: Individualised training plan; 6-12 month rotations offered in CHUV anaesthesiology and adult intensive care and other institutions
Eligibility: Prior postgraduate training in paediatrics strongly recommended; double specialist title (intensive care plus paediatrics or paediatric anaesthesiology) recommended
Accreditation: Recognised category A unit for postgraduate intensive care training (SIWF/ISFM)
Summary: Category A postgraduate paediatric intensive care training at CHUV's multidisciplinary university PICU for children aged 0-18, with individualised training plans and rotations in partner units in Switzerland and abroad.

title: Fellow Neonatal Intensive Care (job advert)
inst: Universitair Ziekenhuis Gent (UZ Gent)
Department: Dienst Neonatale Intensieve Zorg, Sector Man Vrouw Kind
Duration: 1 year (full-time, temporary contract as kliniekarts fellow, grade AG10)
Eligibility: Legal medical diploma and recognised in Belgium as specialist in paediatrics; seeking additional NICU expertise or the special professional title in neonatology
International applicants: Not stated on official page (Belgian recognition as paediatric specialist required)
Funding: Salary per grade and seniority plus on-call allowance
Summary: One-year fellowship at staff level in UZ Gent's 42-bed NICU caring for about 650 newborns a year, including neonatal transport and pre/post-operative care for congenital heart surgery.

title: Postgraduate Training in Paediatric Cardiology and Paediatric Intensive Care (Weiterbildung Kinderkardiologie / Pädiatrische Intensivmedizin)
inst: Herz- und Diabeteszentrum NRW (HDZ NRW), Universitätsklinik der Ruhr-Universität Bochum
Duration: Paediatric cardiology 2 years; paediatric intensive care 2 years (authorised training periods); general paediatrics 3 years
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Accreditation: Training authorisation (Weiterbildungsbefugnis) for paediatrics, paediatric intensive care medicine and paediatric cardiology; certified EMAH (adults with congenital heart disease) centre
Summary: Authorised postgraduate training in paediatric cardiology and paediatric intensive care at the Centre for Congenital Heart Disease of HDZ NRW, with EMAH training and research in collaboration with Ruhr-Universität Bochum.

title: Pediatric Nephrology Residency and Fellowship Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO) / University of Ottawa
Department: Division of Nephrology, Department of Pediatrics
Eligibility: Completed core training in pediatrics; eligible for support by the Ontario Ministry of Health or by their institution
International applicants: Programme consistently has international fellows supported by their governments; foreign applicants see uOttawa PGME website
Accreditation: Fully accredited by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada
Visa support: Applicants must hold a valid Canadian visa
Licence requirement: Not stated on official page (College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario educational licensure applies to postgraduate trainees)
Summary: Royal College-accredited pediatric nephrology training at CHEO for clinical or research careers, including a mandatory one-month transplant rotation at SickKids.

title: Pediatric Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO) / University of Ottawa
Duration: 2 years (possible third year for research/academic pursuits)
Eligibility: Completed at least three core years of pediatrics in an accredited Canadian or US programme, or certification in general surgery, emergency medicine, anesthesia or internal medicine with sufficient pediatric experience
International applicants: IMGs enrolled in Canadian pediatric residency programmes eligible; sponsored (foreign government) residents not eligible via CaRMS; other backgrounds considered case by case
Accreditation: Leads to eligibility for RCPSC subspecialty examination in Pediatric Critical Care
Licence requirement: Not stated on official page (College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario educational licensure applies to postgraduate trainees)
Summary: Two-year PCCM fellowship at CHEO, the lead pediatric trauma hospital for the Ottawa region, preparing trainees for the Royal College subspecialty exam and academic careers.

title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Subspecialty Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO) / University of Ottawa
Department: Division of Emergency Medicine, Department of Pediatrics
Eligibility: Completed three years of core training in pediatrics or adult emergency medicine
Accreditation: Fully accredited by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada; graduates eligible for the PEM subspecialty examination
Licence requirement: Not stated on official page (College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario educational licensure applies to postgraduate trainees)
Summary: Two-year RCPSC-accredited PEM programme based at CHEO, a level-one paediatric trauma centre with about 70,000 annual emergency visits, with trauma and toxicology rotations in Toronto.

title: Pediatric Hematology/Oncology Fellowship Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO) / University of Ottawa
Duration: 3 years (2 clinical years plus a research/focused training year)
Eligibility: Completed three years of core pediatrics or internal medicine at an approved institution
Accreditation: Fully accredited by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada
Licence requirement: Not stated on official page (College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario educational licensure applies to postgraduate trainees)
Summary: Comprehensive clinical and academic fellowship in pediatric hematology/oncology at CHEO with a third year for research or focused training such as stem cell transplantation or neuro-oncology.

title: Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine Training Program
inst: Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO) / University of Ottawa
Department: Division of Neonatology (CHEO NICU and The Ottawa Hospital General Campus)
Duration: 2-3 years (academic); 1-2 years for non-academic role; clinical fellows may be accepted for one or more years
Eligibility: RCPSC certification in pediatrics or at least 3 years of a Royal College-approved pediatrics programme for subspecialty certification; clinical fellows accepted without RCPSC certification
International applicants: Open to trainees from around the world; foreign applicants apply via the University of Ottawa application system
Application method: Canadian-trained residents via CaRMS; foreign applicants via uOttawa application system
Licence requirement: Not stated on official page (College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario educational licensure applies to postgraduate trainees)
Summary: Two- to three-year neonatal-perinatal programme across two level 3 NICUs (CHEO and the regional perinatal centre) designed to train academic neonatologists, welcoming trainees from around the world.

title: General Academic Pediatrics Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO) / University of Ottawa
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: One- to two-year fellowship consolidating pediatric hospitalist and consultant skills with academic training in education, research, administration or public health, and an option to pursue a Master's degree.

title: Pediatric Cardiology Fellowship
inst: Johns Hopkins Children's Center (Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine)
Duration: 3 years minimum (provisional fourth research year available)
Deadline: 31 December of the year preceding the start of fellowship
Eligibility: Applicants in an accredited pediatric residency with preliminary training qualifying for ABP board certification in pediatrics and pediatric cardiology
Application method: ERAS; NRMP (spring cycle); applications complete by 31 December of the year preceding start
Summary: Three-year training programme in academic, research and clinical pediatric cardiology in the division founded in 1931 by Dr Helen Taussig.

title: Pediatric Endocrinology Fellowship
inst: Johns Hopkins Children's Center (Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine)
Department: Division of Pediatric Endocrinology and Diabetes
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Fellowship in the division where Lawson Wilkins began pediatric endocrinology training in 1946, offering diverse training in common and rare pediatric endocrine disorders and cutting-edge research.

title: General Academic Pediatrics Fellowship
inst: Johns Hopkins Children's Center (Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine)
Department: Division of General Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine
Duration: 3 years for physicians without a graduate public health degree; 2 years for those with a doctoral research degree
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-accredited pediatric or medicine-pediatrics residency, or a PhD in a related discipline; fellows at Yard 56 Pediatrics must be bilingual in Spanish
Funding: Funded by institutional and NIH training funds (some trainees supported by a cross-institutional T32)
Summary: APA-accredited fellowship providing training in primary care and population/health disparities research, with resources of the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.

title: Pediatric Hospital Medicine Fellowship Program
inst: Johns Hopkins Children's Center (Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Two-year ACGME-accredited fellowship producing academic leaders in pediatric hospital medicine, with community hospital experience at Johns Hopkins Bayview.

title: Pediatric Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Johns Hopkins Children's Center (Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Funding: Not stated on official page (programme includes a Master of Health Science in Clinical Epidemiology at the Bloomberg School of Public Health)
Summary: Three-year programme combining clinical nephrology, dialysis and transplant care with a Master's in Clinical Epidemiology at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.

title: Pediatric Pulmonary Fellowship
inst: Johns Hopkins Children's Center (Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine)
Department: Eudowood Division of Pediatric Respiratory Sciences
Eligibility: MD, MBBS or DO degree and completed ACGME-accredited pediatrics residency (select PhD applicants considered for post-doctoral work)
Application method: ERAS, from mid-July of the year before the desired start
Funding: Funded by an NHLBI T32 grant; fellows funded for all three years
Summary: ACGME-accredited, T32-funded pediatric pulmonology fellowship personalised to fellows' needs, with a supportive faculty and comprehensive training.

title: Pediatric Cardiology Fellowship Program
inst: Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital
Department: Johns Hopkins All Children's Heart Institute
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Three-year ACGME-accredited fellowship with individualised academic, research or clinical tracks covering imaging, catheterisation, electrophysiology, ACHD, transplant and a busy CVICU.

title: Pediatric Endocrinology Fellowship Program
inst: University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital (Michigan Medicine)
Eligibility: Completed three-year pediatric residency at an ACGME-accredited institution
International applicants: Programme can only accept US citizens or permanent residents because of funding sources; otherwise fellows must provide funding from other sources for the three years
Application method: ERAS from August for 1 July start the following year; personal statement, USMLE transcript, photo, CV, ECFMG transcripts if applicable, three letters
Visa support: Not stated on official page (funding restricted to US citizens/permanent residents)
Summary: Three-year pediatric endocrinology fellowship with inpatient and outpatient training, endocrine and diabetes continuity clinics and broad research opportunities at Mott Children's Hospital.

title: Pediatric Cardiology Fellowship Program
inst: University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital (Michigan Medicine)
Department: Congenital Heart Center / Division of Pediatric Cardiology
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Nationally renowned three-year fellowship at the Congenital Heart Center using a graduated autonomy approach to develop outstanding academic pediatric cardiologists.

title: Pediatric Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital (Michigan Medicine)
Department: Division of Pediatric Critical Care Medicine
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Application method: ERAS (opens 1 July; CV, personal statement, 3 letters, transcript, USMLE transcript) and NRMP; interviews September-October
Summary: ACGME-accredited three-year PCCM fellowship based in a 30-bed PICU and 30-bed Pediatric Cardiothoracic Unit with nationally recognised ECMO, with options for Master's-level training.

title: Pediatric Gastroenterology Fellowship Program
inst: University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital (Michigan Medicine)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Three-year ACGME-accredited clinical and research fellowship for those pursuing academic careers or clinical leadership in pediatric gastroenterology.

title: Pediatric Infectious Diseases Fellowship Program
inst: University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital (Michigan Medicine)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: Three-year programme combining consultation service time at Mott Children's Hospital with a research project, preparing fellows for ABP certification in pediatric infectious diseases.

title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship
inst: Seattle Children's Hospital / University of Washington
Eligibility: Minimum three years of training in an ACGME-approved pediatric or emergency medicine residency
International applicants: International applicants: contact programme director (Seattle Children's fellowships page)
Application method: ERAS (personal statement, 3 letters, board scores) and NRMP Specialties Matching Service
Summary: PEM fellowship training future leaders across Seattle Children's, Harborview Medical Center and UW Medical Center, with PECARN research network participation.

title: Pediatric Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Seattle Children's Hospital / University of Washington
Eligibility: Completion of ACGME pediatric residency; board eligibility in pediatrics
Accreditation: Leads to Sub-board eligibility in Pediatric Nephrology
Funding: Fellows meeting NIH requirements can apply for a position on the NIH TL1 Training Grant
Summary: Pediatric nephrology fellowship established in 1989 with Academic and Clinical tracks and pathways in transplant, dialysis, hypertension, glomerulonephritis, critical care nephrology and more.

title: Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine Fellowship
inst: Seattle Children's Hospital / University of Washington
Eligibility: Completed or on track to complete 3 years of ACGME-approved pediatric residency
Application method: ERAS and NRMP; personal statement, CV and 3-4 letters (one from residency leadership, at least one from a neonatologist)
Summary: Neonatal-perinatal fellowship training neonatologists since the 1960s, with POCUS training, scholarly tracks and clinical time in the Seattle Children's quaternary NICU with neonatal ECMO and dialysis.

title: Pediatric Rheumatology Fellowship
inst: Seattle Children's Hospital / University of Washington
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Application method: ERAS (opens June 2026 for July 2027 start; applications accessed from 15 July 2026) and NRMP; virtual interviews September-October
Summary: Three-year ACGME-accredited fellowship with broad clinical exposure across Seattle Children's, UW Medical Center and Alaska Native Medical Center, and multidisciplinary specialty clinics.

title: Pediatric Hospital Medicine Fellowship
inst: Seattle Children's Hospital / University of Washington
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Summary: The region's only ACGME-accredited academic PHM fellowship, with community rotations in Alaska, Montana and Washington and an optional master's certificate in public health and epidemiology.

title: Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine Fellowship
inst: Nationwide Children's Hospital / The Ohio State University
Eligibility: Completed three years of ACGME-approved pediatric residency and eligible for ABP certifying exam; USMLE Parts 1-3 within Ohio's seven-year time frame (or equivalent)
International applicants: Graduates of schools outside US/Canada/Puerto Rico need a valid ECFMG certificate
Visa support: Foreign medical graduates on a visa should hold a J-1 visa (approval from DIO and programme director)
Summary: Three-year ACGME-accredited fellowship preparing fellows for academic neonatology, with perinatal medicine, neonatal cardiology and protected scholarly time.

title: Pediatric Cardiology Fellowship
inst: Nationwide Children's Hospital / The Ohio State University
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: International graduates accepted with J-1 visa
Funding: T32 grant available to train clinician scientists
Visa support: Foreign medical graduates must hold a J-1 visa (approval by the Designated Institutional Official and programme director required); Nationwide Children's does not sponsor H-1B visas
Summary: ACGME-accredited fellowship offering a well-rounded experience in pediatric and adult congenital cardiology at an internationally recognised Heart Center.

title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship
inst: Nationwide Children's Hospital / The Ohio State University
Eligibility: Graduates of pediatric or emergency medicine residencies (ACGME, RCPSC or CFPC-accredited); board eligible or certified in Pediatrics or Emergency Medicine
International applicants: Foreign medical graduates need ECFMG status report and J-1 visa
Application method: ERAS (opens July): CAF, USMLE scores, 3 letters, CV, personal statement
Visa support: J-1 visas are the only visas accepted
Summary: PEM fellowship in one of the busiest pediatric EDs in the US (62 beds, over 90,000 visits a year; Level I Trauma Center), with a four-year combined Child Abuse/PEM option.

title: Advanced Noninvasive Cardiac Imaging Fellowship
inst: Nationwide Children's Hospital / The Ohio State University
Eligibility: Completed or on track to complete a three-year core pediatric cardiology fellowship in an accredited programme
Application method: CV and application to programme director
Visa support: Foreign medical graduates must hold a J-1 visa (approval by the Designated Institutional Official and programme director required); Nationwide Children's does not sponsor H-1B visas
Summary: Fully funded senior fellowship offering advanced training in transthoracic, transesophageal and fetal echocardiography, cardiac MRI and CT.

title: Pediatric Interventional Cardiology Fellowship
inst: Nationwide Children's Hospital / The Ohio State University
Eligibility: ABP board certified in pediatrics and board certified/eligible in pediatric cardiology; preference to internal applicants; offering based on funding
Application method: CV, cover letter and personal statement emailed to programme director and coordinator; interviews in the fall
Summary: Advanced one- to two-year fellowship in pediatric and congenital interventional cardiac catheterisation across two biplane labs performing 500-550 cases a year.

title: Developmental-Behavioral Pediatrics Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital Colorado / University of Colorado School of Medicine (CU Anschutz)
Eligibility: Completed three years of core pediatrics training
Accreditation: Approved by the ACGME Pediatric Residency Review Committee; provides experience for Sub-Board certification in DBP
Funding: Funded at CU SOM Department of Pediatrics PL4-6 salary levels with full benefits
Summary: Three-year ACGME-approved DBP fellowship at a tertiary referral centre for the Eastern Rocky Mountain region, with LEND participation and mentored scholarly projects.

title: Pediatric Rheumatology Fellowship Program
inst: Children's Hospital Colorado / University of Colorado School of Medicine (CU Anschutz)
Duration: 3 years (clinical first year, two scholarship years)
Eligibility: MD or DO from an accredited institution; ABP board eligible or certified
Application method: ERAS (review begins July; virtual interviews August-October): personal statement, CV, USMLE/COMLEX scores, transcript, MSPE, three letters
Positions: Generally 2 new fellows per academic year
Summary: ACGME-accredited fellowship training outstanding pediatric rheumatologists with multidisciplinary uveitis, CNO, renal and pulmonary clinics and research across CU Anschutz.

title: Pediatric Hospital Medicine Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital Colorado / University of Colorado School of Medicine (CU Anschutz)
Eligibility: Completing or completed a 3-year ACGME-accredited pediatric residency; must have passed USMLE Step 3 or COMLEX Level 3
International applicants: Non-US applicants must hold a valid ECFMG certificate; ACGME requires pediatric residency in a US or Canadian accredited programme before subspecialty fellowship
Application method: ERAS; interview invitations on a rolling basis after 15 July 2026; virtual interviews September-October 2026
Summary: PHM fellowship for self-directed learners combining quaternary and community hospital medicine experience with scholarship, education and leadership training.

title: Neonatal-Perinatal Fellowship
inst: Children's National Hospital (with George Washington University)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Funding: Additional annual stipend of USD 5,657 for programmes requiring in-house 24/7 coverage, including Neonatology (GME candidates page)
Visa support: Children's National processes the J-1 (Alien Physician) visa sponsored by ECFMG (requires USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 CK, ECFMG certification and Ministry of Health Statement of Need); valid EAD from F-1 OPT also accepted (GME candidates page)
Summary: Three-year programme training physician scientists across Children's National's 70-bed Level 4 NICU with ECMO and George Washington University Hospital's Level 3 NICU with over 3,000 deliveries a year.

title: Prenatal-Neonatal Neurology and Neurocritical Care Fellowship
inst: Children's National Hospital (with George Washington University)
Department: Developing Brain Institute / Division of Neurology
Eligibility: Completed residency in child neurology or neurodevelopmental disabilities, or fellowship in neonatology, with demonstrated interest in the immature brain
Accreditation: Accredited by the United Council for Neurologic Subspecialties (UCNS) for Neonatal Neurocritical Care
Positions: 2 positions each year (clinical track); separate NIH T32 clinical research track
Visa support: Children's National processes the J-1 (Alien Physician) visa sponsored by ECFMG (requires USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 CK, ECFMG certification and Ministry of Health Statement of Need); valid EAD from F-1 OPT also accepted (GME candidates page)
Licence requirement: Full licensure to practise medicine in the United States required
Summary: Two-year fellowship in fetal and neonatal neurology and neonatal neurocritical care, with an 80% clinical track preparing fellows for UCNS certification and an NIH T32 research track.
